item.description: Así lo recoge una encuesta de Prima Seguros realizada en colaboración con Nielsen. El 60,7% de los españoles ha contratado alguna vez un seguro por recomendación de familiares o amigos, aunque el 57% de quienes han seguido este consejo también contrasta la información antes de decidir.

item.title: 3M to Argue Australia’s $1.4 Billion ‘Forever Chemicals’ Lawsuit Legally Flawed
item.description: conglomerate 3M plans to argue a landmark case brought by Australia over contamination from the company’s use of PFAS “forever chemicals” in its firefighting foam is legally flawed, a court heard on Friday. The claim against the Minnesota-based chemicals maker and its local unit is the largest ever brought by Australia, and seeks more than A$2 billion ($1.38 billion) in damages for past and future costs of contamination across 28 military bases where 3M’s products were used. Australia’s case is that 3M knew or ought to have known the foam it made and supplied could damage the environment and harm people, but it failed to warn the government.

item.title: The Importance of Patience, Persistence, and Proper Documentation in Surveillance Investigations
item.description: While surveillance is often associated with capturing a single significant moment on video, successful investigations frequently depend on something far less dramatic: patience, persistence, and the ability to recognize meaningful activity as it unfolds. View Series In the field of insurance investigations, surveillance can play a critical role in providing claims professionals with objective information when evaluating reported injuries and physical limitations. As a private investigator, I have learned that some of the most reliable documentation results from remaining observant, maintaining appropriate positioning, and recognizing that a subject’s activities can change unexpectedly throughout the day.

item.title: Why Medical Record Review Shouldn’t Restart When New Records Arrive
item.description: Whether your medical record review runs on AI, people or both, the process should answer one question: What’s new since I last looked? View Series New medical records can come in months or years after a claim opens, so a summary that was written in March may be out of date by July. For claims managers looking at new technology and existing processes, it’s worth testing how the review holds up after several rounds of new records to see whether earlier work carries forward or the process starts over each time.

item.title: Clear exit terms and liquid collateral key to lowering casualty sidecar tail risk charges: AM Best
item.description: As casualty sidecars continue to gain traction, rating agency AM Best has highlighted that clear exit mechanics, high-quality collateral, and transparent risk transfer are critical to lowering tail risk capital charges for sponsors, warning that uncertain exit terms or weak collateral can leave cedents holding unexpected residual risk. The agency importantly states that tail risk matters on both sides of casualty sidecar transactions, given that investors want finality, and cedents want to know what risks (if any), are commuted back to them when an exit is exercised. AM Best added that Compre participates in a defined portion of the George Street Re sidecar, helping shape the contractual terms and the collateral construct that will govern at exit, and is positioned to step into the other investors’ positions over roughly five to seven years, with the ability to take on their future liabilities annually.

item.title: NMS Capital launches specialty MGA, Ascendra
item.description: Private equity firm NMS Capital Group has launched Ascendra Specialty Inc., a technology-driven, full-service managing general agency and program manager. NMS said Ascendra’s launch builds on its insurance-sector strategy of developing dedicated platforms to deploy capital across targeted segments of the insurance and reinsurance markets. According to the firm, Ascendra will initially focus on approximately eight dedicated business lines ranging from Professional Liability, Workers Comp, Transportation, Cyber, Construction, Property, Environmental and Small Business/Specialty.

item.description: Legacy acquirer DARAG Group has completed the transfer of third-party liability reinsurance portfolio from DVA Reinsurance dac (DVA Re), a captive reinsurance vehicle of German mobility and rail logistics group Deutsche Bahn AG. In May 2026, DARAG Deutschland AG completed a portfolio transfer agreement (PTA), approved by the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin), acquiring Ambra’s entire worldwide liability reinsurance portfolio c overing underwriting years from the 1970s to the 2010s. “This transaction demonstrates DARAG’s ability to deliver tailored legacy solutions for captive reinsurers, helping counterparties meet their strategic objectives.

item.title: Reuters: DXC in Advanced Talks to Sell Insurance Software Unit for $2.4 Billion
item.description: IT services company DXC Technology is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Eldridge is discussing combining the business with Zinnia, its insurance technology platform that provides software and digital infrastructure to life insurance and annuity providers, the sources said. Its insurance division offers policy administration systems and other software and business process services to insurers across life, wealth, property and casualty markets.

item.title: Florida OIR Marks End to American Mobile, Which Briefly Served Stressed MH Market
item.description: Six years after it launched and two years after it exited the distressed Florida market, American Mobile Insurance Exchange has officially lost its authority to operate. The Florida-only American Mobile exchange brought some much-needed coverage to the mobile home market in Florida. American Mobile “will offer affordable insurance solutions to a market that historically has been underserved,” LeGare told Insurance Journal shortly after the firm opened for business, in early 2021.

item.title: Supreme Court to Weigh Case Over Race and School Admissions
item.description: The US Supreme Court agreed to consider making it easier to challenge public school admissions policies as racially discriminatory in a fresh test of educational diversity efforts. Racial-preference opponents are seeking to extend the Supreme Court’s 2023 decision barring universities from using race in admissions for the sake of diversity. The school district urged the Supreme Court not to hear the case, saying the 4th Circuit correctly concluded that the policy doesn’t violate the Constitution’s equal protection clause.

item.title: BackNine connects its insurance platform to AI assistants
item.description: BackNine now allows agents to connect their accounts to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, giving them access to its BOSS and Quote & Apply platforms through plain-language requests. Agents can also request life insurance quotes, start applications and email them to clients. The integration uses a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which lets AI assistants access tools in other systems.

item.title: SureEV is building an EV insurance comparison platform
item.description: SureEV is developing an insurance comparison and education platform for electric vehicle owners. SureEV says it does not underwrite policies or currently sell insurance directly. SureEV LLC filed a trademark application for its name on October 16, covering insurance information and planned insurance agency, brokerage and consultancy services.

item.title: Fend targets business risks with event-based protection
item.description: Fend , previously known as Bayes, is building financial protection for businesses exposed to airspace closures, regulatory changes, geopolitical disruption and extreme weather. Fend says it works with businesses to identify events that could disrupt their operations and structure protection around them. It also targets brokers seeking options for risks traditional insurance does not cover.

item.title: California Adds Voluntary Review Before Insurers File Rate Applications
item.description: Insurers seeking personal and commercial lines rate changes in California can go through a voluntary review process that makes the California Department of Insurance’s initial rate analysis public before they formally file rate applications. The regulation is designed to complement the department’s Complete Rate Application Regulation, which requires insurers to provide comprehensive information before applications are publicly noticed. California Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara on Monday introduced the Comprehensiveness Review Regulation, which allows the CDI to publish initial rate range indications, issues identified in insurer submissions and projected premium savings from its review.

item.title: Arity to Acquire INRIX
item.description: (Image source: INRIX website.) Arity (Chicago), a subsidiary of The Allstate Corporation, has agreed to acquire substantially all the assets of INRIX , a provider of transportation intelligence and mobility analytics. Arity says the acquisition will combine its driving-behavior and risk data with INRIX’s transportation intelligence, giving the company a broader view of how people, vehicles, goods and road systems interact. “By combining Arity’s predictive insights on driving behavior and risk with INRIX’s transportation intelligence and mobility analytics, we will be uniquely positioned to deliver more robust intelligence and insights into how people, vehicles, goods, and roads interact.” Broadening Transportation Intelligence The acquisition extends Arity beyond its existing emphasis on driving behavior toward a broader transportation-intelligence platform.

item.title: Uber Wins Bid to Dismiss £250 Million Black Cab Driver Suit
item.description: won a bid to dismiss a £250 million ($333 million) lawsuit after a judge ruled that the claim on behalf of thousands of London’s black cab drivers was filed too late. The claim, filed in 2024 on behalf of more than 13,000 taxi drivers, alleged that Uber improperly obtained a license to operate in London and that it unlawfully took business away from traditional taxi operators. Black cab drivers could have discovered the publicly available material needed to bring the lawsuit by February 2018, the judge said in the ruling handed down on Monday.

item.title: Isaias: 47,000 Claims and $582M in Losses in Florida So Far, OIR Reports
item.description: The late-season hurricane known as Isaias has so far produced about 47,000 claims in Florida, with estimated insured losses at $582 million, carriers have reported to the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation. 9, the numbers compare to Hurricane Sally, which hit nearly the same area in 2020 and produced 72,000 claims and $577 million in losses within six weeks. Most of the Isaias claims have come from residential property owners.

item.title: More Roller Coasters Shut Down as Authorities Probe Fatal Fall Off Georgia Ride
item.description: A growing number of amusement parks have shut down roller coasters as police and state regulators investigate what caused a man to fall out of his seat and plummet to his death at a Georgia park. Summer Bates, who was at the Georgia park with her husband and three children and saw Kariem fall, told the AP previously that her older two children kept trying to push their restraints down tighter while on the ride. Sea World Orlando in Florida and La Ronde theme park in Montreal, Canada, confirmed on Thursday they had temporarily closed rides, bringing the total number of roller coasters halted to 11.

item.title: Insurance, Maintenance Factors Challenge U.S. Plans to Ease Shadow Fleet Sanctions
item.description: Shadow fleet ships still face sanctions from other countries and lack the certification, insurance and maintenance needed to enter mainstream trade. The Department of Energy said any move to ease sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia ⁠move oil or oil products. A potential Trump administration plan to ease sanctions on vessels that have transported sanctioned oil and fuel would likely have limited impact on boosting tanker availability, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

item.title: Monster Tsunami Sent Water 1,580 Feet Up an Alaskan Mountain
item.description: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area on the evening of Aug. In a new study with colleagues, they detail how that landslide sent water and debris 1,580 feet (481 meters) up the other side of the fjord – higher than the top floor of the Taipei 101 skyscraper – and then continued down Tracy Arm. Twelve hours later, a landslide from the adjacent mountain unexpectedly collapsed into the fjord, initiating the second-highest tsunami in recorded history.

item.title: Franklin Templeton moderates cat bond conviction to overweight, turns neutral on ILS
item.description: Franklin Templeton Investment Solutions, the hedge fund-focused arm of the global asset manager, has moderated its stance on the catastrophe bonds asset class slightly from ‘strongly overweight’ to ‘overweight’ for Q4 2026, which in turn has led the firm to shift its stance on the insurance-linked securities market to ‘neutral’. Commenting on the cat bond market’s performance in the third quarter of 2026, Franklin Templeton said, “Although there were several notable catastrophe events in August, none resulted in major insured losses affecting the cat bond market. Combined with seasonal factors, cat bond prices stayed strong as the market approached the peak of the Atlantic hurricane season.” Franklin Templeton also acknowledged that global insured catastrophe losses remained relatively moderate in the first half of 2026, with industry estimates sitting below long-term averages.

item.title: Hannover Re sees ILS capital as sustainable reinsurance addition, source of growth: Horstmann
item.description: Speaking earlier today during Hannover Re’s Baden-Baden media briefing, Patrick Horstmann Managing Director, and Head of insurance-linked securities (ILS) at the firm, emphasised that the German reinsurer sees ILS capital as a sustainable addition to the global reinsurance market and a key area of growth for the company. Meanwhile, it’s roughly 18% of the overall reinsurance capacity, and we see alternative capital as a sustainable addition to the traditional capital in the market,” Horstmann explained during the briefing. “Since November last year, we have launched an insurance agent in Bermuda called Hannover Re Capital Partners, and that is a platform where we connect third-party capital with the risk, utilising our Hannover Re underwriting, modeling, structuring expertise, and so enabling third-party investors to access traditional reinsurance risk with the help of Hannover Re and the support of Hannover Re,” Horstmann added.

item.title: France riots put SRCC accumulation risk in focus for re/insurers: Morningstar DBRS
item.description: France’s latest riots are expected to cost insurers no more than €1 billion-€1.2 billion, according to Morningstar DBRS, assuming no further violence. The agency says the unrest reinforces the need to treat strikes, riots and civil commotion (SRCC) as an accumulation risk requiring dedicated pricing, limits and reinsurance. Assuming no further violence, we expect the latest French riots to be a manageable earnings event rather than a capital event for the country’s major insurers, particularly after reinsurance recoveries and potential claims against the French State,” Marcos Alvarez, Global head of Insurance, Morningstar DBRS, explained.

item.title: Femia to lead newly launched DOXA Re as President
item.description: Adding: “DOXA Re brings together experienced underwriting, analytics and DOXA’s operational resources to move quickly and thoughtfully to meet the needs of carriers and MGAs.” James Femia will lead DOXA Re as President, bringing 22 years of property reinsurance underwriting and leadership experience to the position. Under Femia’s leadership, DOXA Re is to establish a balanced portfolio spanning multiple risk classes, product lines, geographic regions, and client segments. DOXA, a US-based managing general underwriter (MGU) platform, has announced the formation of DOXA Re, a specialty property reinsurance MGU focused on quota share and related proportional solutions for traditional insurers, hybrid carriers and managing general agents (MGAs).

item.title: Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften
item.description: Insurers should treat reinsurance as a capital management tool rather than simply a form of protection, according to Howden Re, which argues that a softening market presents an opportunity to reassess risk retention and improve returns. Howden Re said the current buyer-friendly reinsurance market, with prices softening, allows insurers to redesign programmes around their capital plans. “The best performers treat reinsurance as a capital tool, not only as protection,” the broker said in a report benchmarking 42 European non-life insurers over 2023-25.

item.title: BNSF Railway Sued for Firing Employee Because of Their Disability
item.description: BNSF Railway Company violated federal law when it fired an employee because of his disability after he requested a reasonable accommodation, the U.S. According to the lawsuit, the employee, who has Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, a genetic condition which can result in painful joints, was hired as a BNSF laborer in Chicago in April 2023. BNSF refused the request, failed to provide any alternative accommodation, and instead fired him, the suit said.

item.title: Industry Panel Highlights Challenges in Selling Cyber Insurance to SMEs
item.description: The disconnect became the focus of a recent industry panel at NetDiligence’s Cyber Risk Summit in Philadelphia earlier this month as experts contemplated growth opportunities for cyber insurance, which still accounts for just a very small portion of overall property/casualty premiums. The problem appears to be getting businesses to understand what they’re buying – and getting insurance agents comfortable selling it. However, right now, businesses do not understand the problem or the benefits of a cyber insurance product because the seller can’t present it an effective way, she said, adding that there is only a “small number of brokers that actually have dedicated experts within the organization.” “Even the ones that [have cyber experts], a lot of times they allow their generalists to handle the whole process.

item.title: Lloyd’s issues framework for broker-originated reinsurance structures
item.description: The framework, published in a market bulletin issued by Rachel Turk, chief of performance and strategy, applies to all broker-originated reinsurance structures seeking approval to operate within Lloyd’s. Lloyd’s has released guidance establishing its regulatory expectations and approval requirements for broker-originated reinsurance structures, in response to growing industry demand for efficient mechanisms connecting capital with reinsurance risk. The guidance follows news of Aon’s partnership with Blackstone on a broker-originated reinsurance structures vehicle codenamed “Cortina”, which sees Aon looking to bring Blackstone into Lloyd’s to back broker-originated business, highlighting capital market demand for diversified insurance returns.

item.title: Howden appoints Enrico Nanni as CEO, Europe
item.description: Howden has announced the appointment of Enrico Nanni as chief executive officer, Europe, effective 1 January 2027. I can think of no one better to lead Europe through the next chapter of our journey.” Enrico Nanni, chief executive officer of Howden Europe, said he was honoured to take on the role. Nanni, currently chief commercial officer, will continue in that role alongside his new responsibilities, and will report to Luigi Sturani, chief executive officer, Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA).

item.title: Seaworthy brings disability insurance estimates to ChatGPT
item.description: Seaworthy Insurance has introduced a ChatGPT app that provides individual disability insurance cost estimates based on a user’s occupation, age, sex, and income. Founded in 2011, the brokerage changed its name from Disability Insurance Agency to Seaworthy Insurance in June 2026. Seaworthy serves high-income professionals across all 50 states and says it has placed more than $5 billion in disability and life insurance protection.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance enters Poland
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance announced its entry into the Polish market and the appointment of Carsten Keune as Country Manager, Poland. In his new position, Carsten will lead BHSI’s business in Poland, and Central & Eastern Europe, shaping its market strategy and building strong relationships with customers and brokers. Across Central & Eastern Europe, BHSI offers a broad range of commercial insurance solutions, including Property, Casualty, Construction, Energy, Executive and Professional Lines, Marine, and Multinational insurance.

item.title: Daiichi Life offers $4.4 billion to buy rest of Challenger
item.description: Daiichi Life Group has offered to buy the rest of Challenger in a deal that values the Australian company at around $5.5 billion. Challenger received an indicative offer from TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty, a unit of Daiichi Life, to acquire the remaining 79.5% of Challenger shares at A$11.80 per share, according to a statement. Daiichi Life began investing in Challenger last year.

item.title: Gregorio Garrido presidirá ACS-CV a partir de 2027
item.description: La Asociación de Corredores de Seguros de la Comunidad Valenciana (ACS-CV) eligió el pasado 15 de octubre a Gregorio Garrido como nuevo presidente. Garrido, de la correduría valenciana Solopólizas, asumirá el cargo de forma efectiva el 1 de enero de 2027.

item.title: El siniestro es el momento de la verdad: gestionar bien también significa no perder el hilo
item.description: Durante buena parte de la relación aseguradora, el servicio que se presta desde la correduría puede permanecer “invisible”. El cliente contrata, renueva, recibe documentación, resuelve alguna consulta y sigue con su actividad. Todo funciona con normalidad y, por eso, apenas se percibe.

item.title: La evolución de la Gobernanza de Productos en Europa: avances y desafíos para España
item.description: La gobernanza de productos se ha consolidado como uno de los pilares del marco regulatorio europeo sobre protección al consumidor. Su objetivo es garantizar que los productos aseguradores sean diseñados, distribuidos, monitorizados y revisados atendiendo a las necesidades de su mercado objetivo durante su ciclo de vida.

item.title: California Hybrid Market Share Hits Record as EV Registrations Decline
item.description: Hybrid vehicles accounted for a record 22.8% of new vehicle registrations in California through the first nine months of the year, a new report shows. Tesla’s ZEV registrations declined 10% through September, but its share of California’s ZEV market rose from 46.4% to 56.5%. The report shows strong hybrid demand, as market share rose from 19.5% in 2025 to 24.1% in the third quarter of 2026.

item.title: Coaster Rider’s Death Puts Spotlight on Safety of Ever More Thrilling Rides
item.description: The horrific death of a man who was ejected from a Six Flags roller coaster in Georgia is drawing attention to the safety of amusement park rides that have become increasingly faster and steeper in their quest for the biggest thrill. Fatal roller coaster accidents are extremely rare, and Georgia officials have said little about why Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old school employee from Atlanta, was thrown from his seat on Monday while riding the Goliath at Six Flags Over Georgia, striking other patrons before falling below the ride. Rather than upside-down loops and corkscrews, the two-decade-old coaster focuses on velocity and downhill plunges.
